title: Align Technology, Inc., Q3 2026 Earnings Call, Oct 28, 2026

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Greetings. Welcome to the Align Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] Please note, this conference is being recorded.
I will now turn the conference over to your host, Shirley Stacy, with Align Technology. You may begin.

segments.speaker: Shirley Stacy
paras: Good afternoon. Thank you for joining us. I'm Shirley Stacy, Vice President of Corporate Communications and Investor Relations. Joining me for today's call is Joe Hogan, President and CEO; and John Morici, CFO. We issued third quarter 2026 financial results today via Business Wire, which is available on our website at investor.aligntech.com. Today's conference call is being audio webcast and will be archived on our website for approximately 1 month.

As a reminder, the information provided and discussed today will include forward-looking statements, including statements about Align's future events, product outlook and financial expectations. These forward-looking statements are only predictions and involve risks and uncertainties that are described in more detail in our most recent periodic reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission available on our website and at sec.gov. Actual results may vary significantly, and Align expressly assumes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement.

We've posted historical financial statements with corresponding reconciliations, including our GAAP to non-GAAP reconciliation, if applicable, and our third quarter 2026 conference call slides on our website under Quarterly Results. Please refer to these files for more detailed information.
With that, I'd like to turn the call over to Align Technology's President and CEO, Joe Hogan. Joe?

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Thanks, Shirley. Good afternoon, and thanks for joining us. On today's call, I'll review our third quarter performance and the growth priorities we're executing across Align. John will then discuss our financial results and outlook for Q4 and fiscal 2026.
Before we start, I'd like to note that we announced our CEO Succession Plan earlier today. I'll return to this topic at the end of the call. For now, let's focus on our third quarter results.

We delivered a solid third quarter results with record doctor submitters, record third quarter, Clear Aligner shipments, improved utilization and broad-based international growth. Worldwide revenue was $1.015 billion, up 1.9% year-over-year or 2.4% at a constant currency and in line with our outlook. Clear Aligner shipments increased 6.6% and to $691,000 at the high end of our expectation for mid-single-digit growth in Q3.

In Systems and Services, revenue was $175.5 million, down $7.6 million year-over-year and generally consistent with the guidance we provided at Q2. Reported revenue continues to reflect a shift towards lower-priced scanner configurations and more flexible acquisition models and stable ASP on a like-for-like basis, while our installed base and customer footprint continue to expand.

From a profitability perspective, non-GAAP gross margin was 70.4%, modestly below our expectation, reflecting higher fuel-related transportation costs. Lower Clear Aligner ASP and the impact of geographic and product mix. Disciplined expense management and productivity improvements contributed to non-GAAP operating profit margin of 24.4% above our outlook.

Overall, Q3 demonstrated our ability to execute in a challenging environment, delivering continued Clear Aligner growth, expanding our digital platform and consumer footprint and improving profitability. We remain focused on continuing to drive growth and building on this progress across several key areas.

We continue to drive adoption utilization across customer channels. That includes increasing utilization among orthodontists, expanding Invisalign adoption among GP dentists and growing with DSOs and strategic accounts. During Q3, a record 91,000 doctors submitted Invisalign cases, up more than 3% year-over-year, while overall utilization increased 3.4%. We are expanding the patients and clinical needs that we address. Younger patients remain one of our largest growth opportunities and were again an important contributor to our Q3 performance. Younger patient shipments increased at a double-digit rate in international markets with strong teen performance across APAC and EMEA.

Our growing patient portfolio, including Invisalign First, Invisalign Pallet Expander in the Nebia advancement with close blocks enables doctors to address younger and more complex patients while expanding the range of orthodontic needs that can be addressed with Invisalign treatment.

Affordability and patient conversion continue to be an important focus for us. Our zero additional aligner offering providing doctors with a greater treatment and pricing flexibility. Outpatient financing and commercial programs are designed to help practices convert more prospective patients. Worldwide 0 AA volume increased triple digits year-over-year during Q3.

We're also continuing to expand the value of the Align Digital platform. The opportunity goes beyond Clear Aligners or scanner placements individually. We are connecting iTero, scanning diagnostics, AI-enabled treatment planning, Invisalign treatment, exo CAD restorative workflows and practice applications to create a more integrated digital workflow for doctors and patients. This also represents a growth opportunity beyond traditional orthodontics.

Through dental laboratories, we can reach GP dentists more broadly and enable digital workflows that integrate tooth movement with sestorative treatment and planning. Invisalign Advanced Restorative Treatment, or ART, as we refer to, is a compelling example of lines expanding its role in comprehensive dentistry, creating new clinical use cases, strengthening ecosystem connectivity and increasing our long-term opportunity across the broader dental marketplace.

Importantly, this approach also aligns with the growing focus on oral health by helping clinicians plan treatment more holistically, recognizing the relationship between tooth position, function, restorative outcomes and long-term patient care. These growth opportunities reinforce one another, expanding our doctor-customer base, increasing utilization, addressing more patients and clinical needs, improving affordability and conversion and deepening adoption of our digital platform. So together, they give us multiple pathways to drive growth across Align.

With that context, let me turn to our regional performance and the commercial priorities we're executing to drive growth. In the Americas, Clear Aligner shipments increased approximately 1.5% year-over-year, reflecting different performance trends across North America and Latin America. For the first time in 6 quarters, North America total orthodontic shipments increased year-over-year, supported by growth from DSOs. North American DSO shipments increased at double-digit rate overall, including growth across both orthodontists and GP customers. While the broader retail channel remains pressured, particularly for GP customers, orthodontist retail shipments improved sequentially in Q3 with teen orthodontist retail shipments also increasing year-over-year. We view the return to the year-over-year orthodontist case growth strong DSO performance and sequential improvements in orthodontic retail as an encouraging indicator, particularly given continued consumer softness.

These early signs of improvement in North America reflect our focus on what we can control, strengthening commercial execution, sharpening our go-to-market strategies and deepening key partnerships to help drive conversion. Through sustained efforts to further this progress, we believe we can -- we will return North America back to growth.

Our collaboration with HFD, Healthcare Finance Direct, integrates patient financing options into the Invisalign workflow to give patients greater payment flexibility and reduce administrative function for practices. We're seeing encouraging early traction with these offerings and are evaluating additional financing opportunities, including our new CareCredit pilot. Patient interest in Invisalign remains strong, but affordability can be a barrier to starting treatment. These initiatives are part of our broader effort to address that barrier and convert more patient interest into treatment starts rather than waiting for consumer environment to improve.

During the quarter, we launched the Shift Happens campaign to consumers to increase adult consumer awareness and Invisalign consideration. Our commercial focus is on helping practices convert that interest into consultation and treatment starts. In Latin America, Clear Aligner growth remained strong across channels, was up double digits year-over-year. DSO shipments increased significantly year-over-year, while retail also grew, including positive performance across both GP, dentists and orthodontists.

Our Latin American priorities are centered on affordability and digital adoption, including expanding DSP availability, advancing Invisalign Pay initiatives and broadening iTero access through additional partners, financing alternatives and scanner configurations.

Turning to EMEA. Clear Aligner shipments increased a double-digit growth rate year-over-year, supported by strong utilization across orthodontists and GP dentists and double-digit DSO growth. Retail was also an important contributor. EMEA retail shipments increased 8% year-over-year with growth across both orthodontists and GP dentist customers.

In EMEA, we are focused on orthodontist utilization, teen and growing patient treatment and clinical education, especially Class II. We're working to expand the GP engagement through digital workflows and broader treatment opportunities, including ARC. With DSOs, we continue to focus on improving conversion and scale adoption across practice locations.
In Systems and Services, our focus is on expanding Illumina PC, targeting competitive and legacy iTero scanner users and expanding submitters through art and third-party partnerships.

In APAC, Clear Aligner shipments were up double digits sequentially and increased year-over-year driven by record doctor submitters and strong younger patient demand. Teen shipments increased double digits year-over-year led by China. Retail was the primary channel growth driver in APAC during Q3. APAC retail shipments increased 16% year-over-year with double-digit growth across both orthodontists and GP dentist customers.

In APAC, we are focused on expanding adoption, improving conversion and strengthening the customer experience. This includes expanding private distributor coverage in China, increasing penetration in lower-tier cities and activating DSOs and accelerating tween and teen treatment. We're also focused on improving patient conversion in Japan through orthodontists growth programs as well as driving iTero initiatives. Across the rest of Asia, our focus is on building on the momentum in higher growth markets, including India, Korea and Taiwan.

Customer experience is also an important growth lever across APAC. We're focused on clinical support, customer service, simplifying commercial processes and improving the digital experience. Together, these actions give us multiple avenues to expand growth across orthodontists, GP dentists, retail practices, DSOs, younger patients and digital workflows.

We continue to see a significant opportunity to expand the Invisalign adoption among GP dentists by connecting orthodontic treatment more closely with restorative and broader oral health care workflows.

GP performance remains variable by market and channel. North America GP retail remains pressured, while EMEA and APAC GP Retail both delivered positive year-over-year growth and North America GP DSO grew double digits. These results reinforce our view that GP adoption can expand through clinical education, affordability, digital workflows and broader restorative treatment opportunities. Art is one example of how we are connecting alignment and restorative treatment planning. Along with iTero, Exo CAD and our broader digital platform, these workflows help us engage GP dentists across a wider range of treatment options and create new opportunities to incorporate Invisalign into sort of patient care.

Turning to Systems & Services. Q3 revenue was $175.5 million, down 7.6% year-over-year. The difference between reported revenue and underlying adoption remains important. This reflects a deliberate strategic shift toward flexible acquisition models rather than weakening demand. Revenue continues to reflect a greater mix of lower price configurations as well as flexible acquisition models, including leasing, financing, rentals and certified preowned systems. The mix of iTero-leased units continues to grow and was up double digits again year-over-year. These customer-focused solutions are designed to lower the initial barrier to adoption, expand our customer footprint and give doctors more ways to access our digital technology. Our focus remains on expanding iTero's reach. And in Q3, the number of scanner units placed, including leased, rented and certified preowned systems, increased double digits year-over-year to more than 157,000 systems globally.

In limited pilot, 11 DSO location practices integrating iTero Illumina with Invisalign practice app increased new patient exam capacity by approximately 15% without adding staff or extending operating hours. Nearly 3/4 of participating locations improved productivity. The long-term value of Systems & Services extends beyond the initial scanner placement, a larger, more engaged and trained installed base creates opportunities to expand adoption of restorative workflows and generate reoccurring software and services revenue.

Before turning the call over to John, I want to briefly update you on our strategic initiatives we discussed last quarter. Following our constructive and ongoing discussions with Elliott Management, the first of our 3 independent directors joined Align Board August. Quentin Blackford, President and CEO of iRhythm Technologies is an accomplished global health care and med tech leader, and we're pleased to welcome him to Align.

Our strategic and operating model review is progressing with work focused on commercial effectiveness, organizational scalability, operating efficiency and resource allocation. We're particularly focused on ways to improve performance in North America, identifying additional margin expansion opportunities without compromising growth. We are incorporating early observations into our planning and operating process, and we'll provide additional detail as objectives are finalized. And we can quantify their expected impact.

The operating improvements we are already delivering also reflect broader work across manufacturing, productivity, automation, treatment efficiency and disciplined resource allocation. Our goal is straightforward: drive profitable growth while building a more efficient and scalable business.
With that, I'll turn the call over to John.

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Thank you, Joe. Before turning to our results, I'd like to express my sincere gratitude for your leadership and partnership over the years as well as your many contributions to Align. Your impact will continue to benefit the company and help shape our future success.
Total revenues for the third quarter were $1.148 billion, up 1.9% year-over-year and in line with our Q3 expectations. On a constant currency basis, total revenue was 2.4% year-over-year.

Q3 Clear Aligner revenue was $839.3 million, up 4.2% year-over-year, primarily reflecting higher volume, price increases, lower net deferrals and higher non-case revenue, partially offset by geographic and product mix, higher discounts and unfavorable foreign exchange. On a constant currency basis, Q3 '26 Clear Aligner revenue was up 4.7% year-over-year.

Clear Aligner revenue per case shipment was $1,215, down 2.3% year-over-year or 1.8% at constant currency, consistent with our expectation, primarily due to mix shift to lower-priced countries and products and higher discounts, partially offset by price increases and lower net deferrals.

Q3 Systems & Services revenue was $175.5 million, down 7.6% year-over-year. Revenue continued to reflect the mix towards lower-priced scanners and flexible acquisition models. On a constant currency basis, Systems & Services revenue was down 7.1% year-over-year. Importantly, like-for-like scanner pricing stabilized during the quarter.

Moving on to gross margin. Third quarter overall gross margin was 68.7%, up approximately 4.5 percentage points year-over-year or 5.3 percentage points at constant currency. Performance primarily reflected operational efficiencies and the absence of significant prior year charges, partially offset by lower ASP, restructuring and other charges and unfavorable foreign exchange.
Importantly, the lower ASP is primarily due to product and geographic mix rather than change in pricing discipline.

On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 gross margin was 70.4%, flat year-over-year and approximately 0.7 percentage points higher at constant currency, but modestly below our outlook of approximately 71%. The variance primarily reflected lower Clear Aligner ASP product and geographic mix and Systems & Services mix, partially offset by manufacturing productivity, automation and lower refinement rates.

Q3 Clear Aligner gross margin was 69.3%, up approximately 4.4 percentage points year-over-year, primarily reflecting operational efficiencies and lower depreciation expense on assets disposed of other than by sale, partially offset by elevated freight costs, restructuring costs and lower ASP. On a constant currency basis, Q3 Clear Aligner gross margin was up 5.2 percentage points year-over-year.

Q3 Systems & Services gross margin was 66.2%, up approximately 4.9 percentage points year-over-year, primarily due to lower restructuring, COGS efficiencies and lower U.S. tariff rates, partially offset by lower ASP. On a constant currency basis, Q3 Systems & Services gross margin was up 5.5 percentage points year-over-year.

Third quarter operating income was $169.2 million, resulting in an operating margin of 16.7%, up approximately 7 percentage points year-over-year or 8.5 percentage points at constant currency. On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 operating margin was 24.4%, up approximately 0.5 percentage points year-over-year and approximately 1.4 percentage points at constant currency.
Disciplined expense management and continued productivity improvements allowed us to exceed our non-GAAP operating margin expectation despite the modest gross margin shortfall.

Our Q3 GAAP effective tax rate was 20.6% compared with 40.1% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily reflecting the prior year impact of restructuring charges in our jurisdictional mix of income and lower U.S. taxes on foreign earnings in the current quarter. Our Q3 non-GAAP effective tax rate was 20%.

Third quarter diluted net income per share was $1.90, up $1.12 compared to the prior year. On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 diluted net income per share was $2.80, up 7.3% year-over-year. GAAP and non-GAAP EPS were unfavorably -- each unfavorably impacted by approximately $0.24 year-over-year from foreign exchange.

As of September 30, cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.145 billion, up approximately $140 million year-over-year. Cash flow from operations was $183.2 million, capital expenditures were $45.1 million and free cash flow was approximately $138 million.

During Q3, we repurchased approximately 627,000 shares at an average price of $164.73 per share, returning $103.3 million to our shareholders. Year-to-date, we have repurchased $200 million of common stock. For fiscal 2026, we expect to repurchase approximately $500 million of common stock, up from $466 million repurchased in 2025 and reflecting the conviction of our Board and management in Align's long-term value.

Now turning to Q4 and fiscal 2026. I am pleased to deliver third quarter revenue and Clear Aligner volume in line with our outlook while improving year-over-year profitability. Consistent with our first and second quarters, these results were achieved against a challenging market backdrop. As demand across the dental and orthodontic industry continued to be affected by a softer environment for discretionary health care spending and capital equipment investment. Those conditions persisted through the third quarter, and our fourth quarter outlook reflects what we continue to see across the broader market.

Our updated 2026 guidance reflects a reduction in expected reported revenue versus our prior outlook provided at Q2, driven by 2 main factors. First, our Q4 Systems & Services revenues outlook is lower than our prior guidance. Although we expect scanner volume growth and solid scanner ASPs stabilize on a like-for-like basis during Q3, product mix continues to shift towards lower-priced scanners and more flexible acquisition models, which resonates well with customers amid a more challenging environment for capital equipment purchases.
Second, we have slightly lowered our Clear Aligner volume as well as ASP assumption, largely driven by product and geographic mix in addition to foreign exchange.

Assuming no circumstances occur beyond our control that could impact our business for Q4 2026, we expect worldwide revenues to be in the range of $1 billion to $1.20 billion. We expect Q4 Clear Aligner volume to be up low single digits year-over-year. We expect Clear Aligner ASP to be down approximately 1% year-over-year. We expect Systems & Services revenue to be in the range of $170 million to $180 million. We expect worldwide GAAP gross margin to be approximately 71% and non-GAAP gross margin to be approximately 72%. We expect GAAP operating margin to be approximately 20%. We expect non-GAAP operating margin to be approximately 26%. For Q4 2026, we expect to repurchase up to $300 million of our common stock.

For fiscal 2026, we expect 2026 worldwide revenue to be approximately $4.11 billion to $4.13 billion. We continue to expect 2026 Clear Aligner volume and revenue growth to be up approximately 5% to 6% year-over-year. We expect 2026 Clear Aligner ASP to be slightly below 2025. We expect 2026 Systems & Services revenue to be $715 million to $725 million. We expect 2026 GAAP operating margin to be approximately 16.2%, up approximately 2.7 points year-over-year. We expect 2026 non-GAAP operating margin of approximately 23.7%, representing approximately 100 basis point improvement year-over-year, consistent with our previous guidance.

We expect capital expenditures of approximately $125 million to $150 million. We expect to repurchase approximately $500 million of our common stock during 2026. As we look to 2027, we believe we are well positioned to deliver another year of revenue growth and margin expansion. Importantly, our preliminary planning assumes an operating environment broadly consistent with current conditions and does not require a consumer recovery. We expect a continued driving Invisalign volume growth in 2027, record doctor submitters improving utilization and the growth initiatives discussed today support that confidence with additional initiatives under development.
We also continue to expect a broadly stable Clear Aligner pricing environment with ASP slightly down, driven primarily by product and geographic mix.

For Systems & Services, 2026 has been a transition year for revenue. We expect solid unit growth and continued expansion of our installed base and we expect stable ASPs positioning Systems & Services for revenue growth in 2027.

On profitability, we continue to target at least another 100 basis points of non-GAAP operating margin improvement in 2027, building on the approximately 100 basis points we expect to deliver in 2026. Our focus is on improving efficiency while preserving investment in the initiatives that support sustainable revenue growth.

Share repurchases should provide an additional benefit to earnings per share growth as we continue to view buybacks as an attractive use of capital at prices that we do not believe reflect Align's long-term value creation potential. We will provide our full 2027 outlook when we report fourth quarter results following the completion of our strategic and operating model review with Jen leading the business.
With that, I'll turn it back to Joe. Joe?

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Let me pause by bringing together what you've heard today. We delivered solid Q3 performance with record third quarter Clear Aligner shipments, record doctors submitters improve utilization continued expansion of iTero customer footprint and stronger operating performance, varied by market and channel. But we also saw important areas of traction, including overall orthodontist growth, strong DSO performance in Latin America, broad-based growth in EMEA and strong retail performance in APAC and America.

While the external environment remains challenging, our results continue to demonstrate that we have meaningful opportunities to improve performance through execution regardless of the pace of the macroeconomic recovery. We're focusing on increasing utilization among orthodontists, expanding Invisalign, adoption among GP dentists, growing with DSOs and strategic accounts, extending our leadership in kids and teens, improving affordability and patient conversion and increasing adoption of our digital workflows.

Across Systems & Services, our priorities are to expand the iTero customer footprint, increased utilization and connect scanning more deeply with diagnostics, treatment planning, restorative workflows and Invisalign treatment across the Align digital platform.

We also have a significant innovation pipeline ahead of us. Across digital treatment planning, AI-enabled capabilities, growing patient treatment, restorative workflows, scanning solutions and CAD/CAM software, we're investing in technologies that can expand clinical applicability, improve the customer experience and make our business more productive at scale.

We continue to be excited about our next-generation direct fab patient 3D printed materials platform, what we call NXT technology. NXT unlocks greater control, consistency and precision across appliance, designS enables an entirely new level of Invisalign performance and personalization. Building on the Invisalign Palate expander, our first direct 3D printed orthodontic appliance, we are broadening the application of 3D printing across the Invisalign portfolio as well as expanding it into new categories.

Invisalign specifics, attachment systems launched this year expands our 3D printing capabilities beyond aligners and appliances into attachment system itself. By conducting digital treatment planning, manufacturing, clinical delivery, it represents another step toward a fully integrated digital workflow.

This week, we will begin a U.S. pilot of a new product category, Sports Mouth Guards powered by our 3D printing technology and material science capabilities. Sports Mouth Guards represent a large and growing market opportunity and then growing awareness of concussion risk and contact sports. There is also a significant overlap with kids and teens as we expect it to drive awareness and utilization of Invisalign treatment through Invisalign doctors while providing incremental revenues.

Invisalign Sports Guard is a custom direct 3D printed sports mouthguard made from an iTero digital scan. It comes in multiple thickness options and will be available through participating Invisalign providers. Invisalign Sports Guards are customizable for each athlete's unique needs for comfort and support. Optimized for high performance specific to the activity, thanks to the power of high-performance polymers and unique 3D printed designs. Expected to offer over time a broader set of diagnostics and other sensing capabilities. These are important steps in a broader road map and includes additional orthodontic applications and the opportunity to apply direct fabrication technology more broadly to aligner treatment. We will continue to advance the road map as we scale the technology and validate each application.

What gives me confidence looking ahead is that we are not dependent on any single growth driver, geography or customer segment. We have opportunities to increase orthodontist utilization, expand GP adoption, grow with DSOs, extend our leadership in kids and teens, improve affordability and patient conversion and increased adoption of the Align Digital platform.

Before we open the call for questions, I want to briefly address my decision to step down and the planned CEO succession announcement we made today. Leading Align has been a tremendous privilege and this is an amazing decision -- a meaningful and amazing decision for me as we move forward. The process has been carefully planned for some time. It reflects a thoughtful long-term focus. As announced, our Board has appointed Jennifer Davis as Align's next CEO. Jen will join us on November 2 as CEO-Elect and a member of our Board. She will assume the CEO and President role on December 31 of this year. Jen brings 33 years of leadership experience, including leading Procter & Gamble's Global Healthcare business, with global experience across innovation, digital transformation, brand building operations and customer development in oral health. Jen will be joining the company with powerful innovation platform, a talented global team trusted relationship with doctors around the world and significant opportunities across orthodontics and digital dentistry.

I'm extremely proud of Align, the strong foundation we've established and the relentless contributions of every member of our Board, management team and organization. I am confident in this transition plan, and I'm looking forward to working closely with Jen over the coming months. I strongly believe she is the right leader to build on that foundation and lead Align through the next phase of growth and value creation.

My focus remains squarely on driving the business, executing the priorities we discussed today and continue to advance the growth, innovation and operating initiatives underway across Align. I remain confident in the opportunities ahead for Align and the team executing our strategy and in our ability to continue to build long-term value for our customers, shareholders and employees.
Thank you for joining us. Operator, we'll now open for questions.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: [Operator Instructions] And our first question comes from Michael Cherny with Leerink Partners.

segments.speaker: Michael Cherny
paras: Joe, best of luck in retirement as you move on. I'll just ask one now. I'm sure there's plenty of others. But as you think about the changing conditions that you saw underlying the difference in views and particularly on case starts between what you saw in 3Q versus what you saw in 4Q, can you give us a sense on what some of the factors were relative to the low single-digit case start expectations? What are you seeing from a leading indicator perspective? Anything else you can point to in terms of the drivers and the build on the 4Q numbers? The 3Q level was very strong across the Board. Curious what you're seeing relative to how the setup is for 4Q, though, as you look to -- into next year?

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Yes. Thanks, Michael. We felt great about our third quarter performance. We see a challenged market really across the globe in so many countries. And as I mentioned in his script and John mentioned in his script, too, we felt really good about being able to deliver in that kind of environment.

As we look at the fourth quarter, we see continued challenged consumer overall. And that's a common theme we see across the Board. I mean obviously, with our Systems & Services business, we have a reorientation that you saw in the third quarter you've seen this year, and that's reflected in our go-forward statement, too. So this is not a singular type of variable that we're discussing here. This is a broad-based, I think, reticent consumer that we sense not just in North America but different parts of the world, and that's being reflected in our guidance.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Jon Block with Stifel.

segments.speaker: Jonathan Block
paras: Joe, I'll start with the question that's likely for you and probably Jennifer as well. The Sports Mouth Guard, I know it's a bit early, but more importantly, just big picture, what does it say about line? Like is this the start of going into adjacencies. You called out mouth guard before -- when you first got there, we heard about sleep apnea -- is this a clear liner company going forward? Is this a 3D printing company going forward? We would just love your thoughts there.

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: John, great question. Look, when I started, obviously, sleep apnea was on a table and I shot that because I felt the technology was diversionary. I thought it was a channel we didn't understand overall. A reimbursement system, we had not a prayer of understanding [indiscernible] sell in the front of a customer. And it was also an item that is very difficult to be able to manufacture and do it in at scale like we have to do. And so I just thought it was a diversion in the sense of what the company would focus on.

As I look at Mouth Guard, John, I can tell you that almost every orthodontist we have out there is asking for Mouth Guards. They feel that's a leader product for them in that team market, especially with schools and different kind of demand profiles with schools and kids in those specific ZIP codes. The reason I want -- I thought it was time to do this is we have a unique resin we've developed. It's has significant advantages over resins that are used for mouth guards today. It's 3D printed.

So the first mouth guard that you can make specifically for certain sports, certain configurations in the way people speak and how they present themselves. It gives you a huge amount of flexibility in the sense of how you can go after that marketplace. Sports Mouth Guard business is anywhere between $6 billion to $8 billion and how you look at it. It's primarily a boil and bike kind of a marketplace. It means non-exact kind of manufacturing science that's used about it. So John, why in this case, unique technology, very unique from a consumer standpoint, right in line with our channels of distribution, right? Our orthos want to have it. GPs wanted too, but orthos also so we can sell it through our current channels without any kind of friction. So I look at it as 180 degrees versus sleep apnea devices.

segments.speaker: Jonathan Block
paras: Great color. And then as a follow-up, John, for the quarter, like case is better, I think, certainly better and better than figured. ASP light, maybe you can give a little bit more on that dynamic because -- and I'm thinking about this correctly, comp no AA is not an upfront ASP hit arguably. And then maybe you could just also touch on the exit rate. I know most of the revisions for 4Q were around Systems & Services and maybe a little FX. But it does seem like you noodle down clear line a bit. So maybe you can just talk about that exit rate there.

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes. Thanks, Jon. I'll start with ASP. Yes. ASPs were above what we expected. We had a little bit of unfavorable FX. We get the continued country and product mix. So 2 of the reasons driving some of that ASP kind of sequentially down really the growth that you see in many of these markets that just have a lower list price. So you see India and China and others that are sequentially and year-over-year growing. That shows up from an ASP standpoint as well as introducing DSP and some of that touch-up cases that we have. We do see that. It's just a low list price product that ends up showing up in ASP, but it was able to help us in the end, drive volume, as we said, and ultimately, deliver the margin that we needed. And that's how we look at that.

I would say when we think about the exit rate and we're factoring in, in our guidance what we saw in Q3, we factor in what we see in October. And that's what we used to inform our guide. So no change in terms of how we do it and what we look at. It's just a reflection of a continued challenging market and things that we're doing to try to help offset it.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Brandon Vazquez with William Blair.

segments.speaker: Brandon Vazquez
paras: Joe, congrats on a great career at Align and good luck on the next steps. I wanted to focus first, let's just kind of double-click on the macro a little bit. I think the prior to -- we're asking something similar to this. But can you talk a little bit more granular about what have things incrementally from Q2 to Q3 on the macro side? Are there any pockets of things getting worse or better?

Joe, I think you had said North America declined in the quarter in your prepared remarks. Did I hear that correctly? And is that -- again, is that better or worse? We don't always get figures like that. So just curious if you can kind of level set us on relative to last quarter, how some of the key geographies are doing.

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Brandon, good question. On -- just start with the U.S. where you started with 2 or North America. I mean we felt good about Latin America and our performance here was great. I was happy to see that we had positive orthodontic growth for the first time in -- I think it's the 6 quarters that we've had in the U.S., which is really positive.

On the GP side, obviously, we saw continued erosion. That's a larger bucket of doctors we have to call on. There's challenges across keeping up with those doctors and pushing those doctors to consumers that we talked about, being a little less reticent, especially in that GP channel to convert. So I feel -- as I mentioned in the script, too, I feel good about our ability to really push on the GP side. You see our DSO business there continues to grow. It's that retail segment that's challenging, in particular GPs that are doing less than 10 cases a year.

And so -- but I feel we've arranged our workforce properly to be able to go after that. We have good early warning signals right now. We're -- we might be losing GPs in different places that we can move our sales force in that way. So I see a challenged market, a challenged consumer, but I feel good about our product base, and I feel good about our ability to address.

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: The products that are really starting to take hold. We talked a lot about the NO AA or reduced the amount of AA type products. They're growing. And across the globe growing at a triple-digit rate, which is great. That's really helping win with doctors, especially in that gray area with that upfront cost. And then we also talked a lot about, and we're seeing more and more, especially in this challenged environment where those potential patients are turning to financing to be able to help them afford that treatment. And you see our partnerships with many finance companies, not just in North America, but it's really now become more across the globe, and that's helping win those gray areas as well with those patients.

segments.speaker: Brandon Vazquez
paras: Got it. And then intra-quarter, we had gotten a lot of questions around China VBP. I know there's some nuances to your exposure to China and then the private versus the public I don't -- hopefully, I didn't miss something in the prepared remarks, but maybe a good opportunity to kind of level set investors what the potential exposure is to China VBP in the orthodontic side. And then also what kind of is the latest in expectations of timing?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes, Brandon, this is John. So VBP will participate in. It's going through its process. I would expect that as things open up into the fourth quarter in terms of products that will be entered into, we'll participate in. As you know, and it's been 1 well documented, it usually starts on the public side. We don't have a lot of exposure on the public side. Only about 15% of our business in China is public. Most of it's private. But we'll participate in that. We think that it helps grow in this market where like we said, from a company standpoint, most of our product is on the private side. But the vast majority of cases done in China are done with wires and brackets.

So if VBP allows more exposure, more people to be able to use Clear Aligners that will help participate and help drive. We feel that with our operations there, our treatment planning, the sales force, everything that we have on a go-to-market standpoint really will help us as we navigate through that process.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Vik Chopra with BMO Capital Markets.

segments.speaker: Vikramjeet Chopra
paras: Joe, best of luck to you, and thanks for all your help. Over the [indiscernible]. The question for me is on 2027 framework that you laid out. You've targeted another 100 basis points of margin improvement without a consumer recovery. Can you talk about the biggest drivers of that? Is this a floor or a base case? And does the Elliott operating review -- is there potential for that to add to that?

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: John?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes. I can start with that, Vik. When we have a lot of productivity and efficiency programs in place. Obviously, we know how to manufacture and manufacture at scale there to drive productivity. So many of the actions that we've been doing for the last several years are coming to fruition, and we're driving that improved productivity. We're seeing that this year. We see the gross margin improvements that we've had in the business. Some of it is product related, where you have that less dependence on these complicated products that have multiple refinements and we go to fewer refinement-type products. That drives a lot of productivity in our business. So some of it is at the product level, some of it's at the initiatives that we have to be able to help drive improvements in productivity.

Of course, we're going through this strategic review and understanding where we could save money, where we could invest to be able to drive growth and do it in a profitable way. So we feel good about the efforts that we have up until this point. We'll continue to make refinements to it. And then at the end of Q4 here, we'll be prepared to talk about what that means for 2027. But we hold to the fact that the op margin improvement next year that we've committed to that at least 100 basis point improvement is progressing well, and we'll update more about what that means for the rest of the P&L next quarter.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Jeff Johnson with Baird.

segments.speaker: Jeffrey Johnson
paras: Joe, again, I'll just add the congrats on a great career and good luck in retirement. Let me ask one follow-up question on VBP, if I could, and then I want to ask a case volume question as well. But John, on VBP, obviously, a lot of moving parts, as you said, maybe getting bigger into the public side if you bid on that side of the business here in this round.

On the private side, we are hearing the Chinese government kind of pushing for private docs to also participate from a pricing perspective in VBP. I guess, net, we don't know how that's going to play out. But should VBP be a good guy, a bad guy for you guys next year, there's all the moving parts on what happens in your private market pricing versus if you get public market incremental volumes? So help us out maybe on just net how we should think about this?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Well, as you're right, there are a lot of moving pieces to it, Jeff. And I think when you look at it as -- if it gets it will get to private as it goes to private. The real question will become is what doctors do with those price differences do they pass them on to the potential patients. We hope they do because that will drive an increased amount of utilization and adoption of Clear Aligners. So we hope that, that's where it ends up going. But we see increased volume that will come through. That's typically what happens to VBP. We think we're properly positioned in China to be able to kind of in China for China to be able to manage the cost.

And I think when you look at it overall from a net-net revenue standpoint, it's to us, it's neutral to positive, just from the standpoint, you're going to drive a lot of volume, I think, as it works its way through the system. And you will have some price, but I think the volume helps offset it. And as long as that product portfolio that we have is in place as well as some of the in-China operations we have, we think we're properly positioned.

segments.speaker: Jeffrey Johnson
paras: All right. Fair enough. And then just on the case volume side, you're guiding low single digits for 4Q. I think when I think about how you guided '26 previously on last quarter's call and guided 3Q on the 2Q call. Feels like that 4Q case volume guidance globally is maybe down 1 point or 2 point relative to what you were thinking? Just taking your pulse on that, is that about right, maybe 1 point or 2 point lighter than you would have been expecting, number one. and you'll hit very similar comps. You hit a 7-plus comp here in the fourth quarter. The next few comps into 27 are going to be similar. Is that kind of low single digit for 4Q against a 7-plus comp about the way we should think about coming up against those other 7% comps through the first few quarters of next year as well?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: You're right from a stack standpoint. The stack is very similar to the 2-year stack that we've seen at Q3 and then kind of the implied guidance for Q4. So you get to that, Jeff. I think what you see is continued consumer that's challenged across many markets. You've got to do a lot of things to try to motivate them to go into treatment when they have that challenge, financing some of the product portfolio and other things that we're trying to do to help with the go-to-market efforts. So slight tweaks that we've made based on what we're seeing on a global basis.

But in that overall revenue that we're talking about for the year of that 5% to 6% and similar amount from a volume standpoint for Clear Aligners. So overall, that hasn't changed too much from a total year standpoint, but just adjusting slightly for Q4.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Elizabeth Anderson with Evercore ISI.

segments.speaker: Elizabeth Anderson
paras: Congratulations, Joe, on your retirement. I wanted to dig in a little bit on the scanner side. I mean if we think about the implied scanner guide, it's a little bit lower, I think, than expectations, but also to Jeff just pointed out, the comps get a lot tougher. So I guess, how do we think about it kind of lapping last year's upgrade sales? You talked about the lower price scanner mix after leasing, some of the capital leasing that you sort of offer? Like I guess, could you help us double-click on some of those different components so we can sort of understand the lay of the landscape for that demand environment and sort of how to think about that going forward?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes. That's a good question, Elizabeth. This is John. So first and foremost, the scanner equipment sales that we have, the unit volume has been very strong. We see the installed base up double digit. So we're getting good adoption of our scanners, and we're very pleased with that. That's a great scanner, great portfolio. We have being able to get to those doctors. Some still want to have the latest and greatest Lumina. All the bells and whistle is great, and that comes through as equipment sell-through.

Some doctors are like, I don't need the full system, I'll do more of a flex model where they just look into a laptop and it fits their needs. Some doctors are looking at maybe the certified preowned. Any which way they want those units, we're happy to sell, just whatever fits their needs. The added component that we see is a lot more leasing, a lot more rental. And those doctors are like, we just, "We want the scanner. I just don't want to pay for it upfront." So we're seeing a those placements happening, you're starting to build up more of that rental income because it's from previous quarter rental revenue that's from previous quarters that's now building up into whatever current quarter you're in as well as leasing and so on. So that's an evolution that continues to happen within the business.

What we saw as we went from second quarter to third quarter, we saw relatively stable pricing on an overall equipment standpoint. So that was a good sign for us that it's kind of more bottomed out there from a price standpoint, and we feel good that we can build off of that for Q4. And more importantly, as we look into 2027, we build off of that to '27 such that we expect Systems & Services to grow next year because the pricing has stabilized because of the trade-offs that are happening between equipment sales and leasing so that when we look at 2027, it's much more stable. And as we've said in the past, as we've talked about, you get about the same growth between the equipment side of our business as well as the Clear Aligner side, and that's what our expectation would be for next year.

segments.speaker: Elizabeth Anderson
paras: And then if we think about that scanner growth and you talked about the switch to [indiscernible], we've obviously historically really nice attach rate of the case growth to those scanner sales. Are you seeing anything different in the attach rate in terms of new cases from one of those placements or leases or secondhand sales as what we've seen historically versus sort of when you just had the prior model of just new sort of sales?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes, what you see is you see doctors who might not have wanted to go and use our scanner. What we see, we talked to about a record number of submitters that we have in the quarter. Some of that is helping by being able to get a scanner that they might not have gone to before. The acquisition cost is less because they're leasing it. It's just this monthly fee that they pay. And then it starts the front end of the digital ecosystem. They're starting to use Invisalign and digitize so that it helps them grow their business in a digital orthodontic way. So we like the combination of being able to help them digitize their practice and really be as efficient and beneficial for their patients as possible.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Jason Bednar with Piper Sandler.

segments.speaker: Jason Bednar
paras: Joe, I'll just echo the congrats there, and pleasure working with you over the past several years. Guys, I do appreciate the color here on 2027. The framework there, maybe I want to layer on to some of the questions earlier. I know this business can be tough to predict at times, but you are throwing out some initial guardrails or floors, whatever you want to call them. What are the macro assumptions you're embedding in that Aligner outlook? Is it more or less status quo for the U.S. and international? And then can you get a little bit more detailed, we've been poking around at some of the different moving parts. But just on the ASP outlook, what are the puts and takes that are contributing to the 2027 framework?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes. When we look at 2027 framework, first off, we're not expecting much of a change in the overall consumer. The consumer will be what it does. It's a challenging environment for inflation and other inputs that those potential patients have. So we're not expecting really a change from that. What we are pushing and helping drive is how do we go to market with various products and combinations to be able to get to our doctors to be able to help them start cases, ultimately do more cases. You couple that with financing to those potential patients, really trying to get those reluctant patients to actually get into treatment. So that's how we're building throughout this year in this challenging environment and what we would expect for next year.

As we think about our growth and what we've seen from a growth this year and our expectation for next year is, look, you're going to see some of those markets where we've had great growth on the international side. I would expect those to continue. India and China and Latin America and others, they're going to continue. Those are great growth opportunities for us. That continues. They come at a lower list price. It's just what the market is. You're also going to see some of these products like the DSP, touch-up cases and so on. That will end up -- we end up growing faster, too. Those 2 combinations, geographic plus product mix, take our ASPs down. And what we've been seeing is that 1% to 2%. This year, it will be down about 1%. But I think from a planning standpoint, to that geographic and product mix about 1% to 2%.

segments.speaker: Jason Bednar
paras: Okay. That's helpful. And maybe I'll follow up just on scanners and services. To follow up on Elizabeth's question previously. Where does the confidence come from the '26 here will be the bottom and that the shift to the alternate purchasing model won't gain further momentum as we move into next year. I guess just wondering where the confidence lies that this isn't some secular shift that you won't see, again, play out again next year.

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Yes. Think about it, Jason, we've got -- from a new product standpoint, we've certainly seen some of that price shifting. And we started seeing this in the first quarter really played out in the second quarter. It was stable in the third quarter, meaning that pricing was about equal, and this is really across the globe. So what we also see is strong demand. There is demand for this product. That installed base growing like it is. The product is well received. All the products that we have are well received. It's just that. In some cases, it's at a lower price. -- but we think that stabilized.

And then when you look at the leasing and rental, some markets have shifted to that. It is in all markets, but in some markets, it shifted to that. And what you do is you just forgo as much -- you don't get as much revenue upfront, but you get that revenue later on. The key for us is we want those doctors to be able to have that scanner at their practice, help them digitize and lead to more use of digital orthodontics and we think that's a good thing. And we're expecting to build on that as we go into 2027.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Steven Valiquette with Mizuho Securities.

segments.speaker: Steven Valiquette
paras: Let me also offer my congrats to Joe on 11-plus years of successful leadership at Align. I guess just for me, again, not to ask too many questions on 2027 overall on this call, but the comment again about expecting it to continue to drive Invisalign volume growth in 2027. I know it's kind of intentionally vague so we have a preliminary view and left wide open to interpretation. So I guess -- I know there's a further message within that? I'm just trying to confirm, maybe yes or no, is there anything structurally that right now that would prevent the growth in 2027 being similar to the mid-single digits you have in 2026 without? Stating the obvious, something like 5% to 10% growth would be phenomenal, but 1% growth while its growth would not be viewed great right now relative to expectations and consensus, et cetera. So hopefully, that question makes sense.

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Look, I think -- Steve, this is John. So when you think of what we're trying to do is, we're expecting a challenging macro environment. I don't know if in Magic gets better into next year. So given that the work that we're doing from the product portfolio and what we're doing to go to market as well as some of that consumer and other financing options to be able to house with those potential patients to go into treatment, it served us well this year. When we think about our Clear Aligner revenue and volume, as we talked about for the full year, that 5% to 6%, that's served us well in 2026.

We'll give more details about what it means for 2027 in light of all the efforts that we have going on. But we feel good about what we're trying to do to try to drive that utilization and adoption go to market because the underlying overall market hasn't changed. The vast majority of cases are still done with wires and brackets, and we have the opportunity to grow in this space. It's just that macro that we have to work against. And that's why we want to make sure that we can continue to grow.

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Yes, I think what I want to emphasize too and just what John's comment because there's a lot of questions about 2027. We're not predicting 2027 is going to fall off in some way. Just like John said, we expect very -- we can't predict what the economy is going to look like. We feel good about our ability to execute in a difficult situation from a consumer standpoint, and we'll continue to execute that way.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Erin Wright with Morgan Stanley.

segments.speaker: Erin Wilson Wright
paras: Congrats, Joe, again. It was great working with you. You mentioned financing a few times now. And I guess, can you speak to some of the newer financing initiatives in terms of where that stands in terms of the rollout of those? And just anything that you can give us in terms of how that's translating into conversion?

And then just a second question just on macro and the pressures that you're seeing. Like what are you seeing in terms of also like share shift back to brackets and wires or something like that? Or is it just purely underlying kind of demand trend and who's walking in the front door?

segments.speaker: John Morici
paras: Maybe I could start with some of the financing. We're seeing many countries and many regions adopting financing, using external financing that really haven't done it before, and we're helping lead the way and do it in a way where we're working with some of these financing companies being able to get them into those offices through our sales team, being able to talk about the financing options. More and more in this environment, people are looking for ways to be able to afford things. And that gets ultimately down to a month-by-month basis.

So I would say, Erin, you're seeing this much broader across the U.S., and it's helping us win those gray areas with those potential patients. And what I'm really encouraged about is we're solving some of these in Europe that we never really thought we could get through. These finance companies are now much more willing to partner with us and be partners with us to be able to help provide financing solutions to consumers. So it's early that we're seeing this, but it's good progress, and we feel good about this as being a differentiator to help, especially in this economy to be able to upgrow the business.

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: And in your second part of your question, Erin, about wires and brackets and how are on remember, majority of the cases we do are adults still. From a team standpoint, we -- you hear more and more about wires and brackets and different things. But as I mentioned in my script, we really feel good about the early intervention that we have. When you look at Invisalign first, you look at IPE, mandibular advancements, those products are growing at double digits for us right now. And it gives us really good access into that teen and tween marketplace overall. So we'll keep pushing those products, and we'll keep driving adults too, and that's -- our shift happens piece is aimed right at that to help the orthodontics grow their the adult side and then also with the GP side also. So I feel good about our go-to-market, both in product and also from a marketing standpoint.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Our next question comes from Kevin Caliendo with UBS.

segments.speaker: Kevin Caliendo
paras: Joe, good luck with everything going forward in case we are passed on crossed again. I wanted to talk about the mouth guard a little bit because it's certainly interesting. Is this a product that do you anticipate distributing through like a retail channel? Meaning are you going to go to DICK'S Sporting Goods and see in Align Mouth Guard? Or is it a mouthguard that's going to be specific for people that might be going through the orthodontists already or GP? Like where is the end user going to learn about these Mouth Guards?

And I guess the pricing strategy here, is this like a premium product versus a generic product because it doesn't sound like generic if you have some kind of resin that's proprietary. And I guess my concern is, if you sell it somewhere that's not in a retail setting, does it potentially impact the retainer business because I'm guessing the pricing of a retainer might be a lot more than a mouth guard. But I'd just love to hear a little bit about the strategy and more about the mouth guard.

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Yes, Kevin, it's a good question. First of all, we won't be selling it directly to consumers. That's not the game. We have the channels that we want to work it through. with orthodontists really asking for this product line because of their strong teen marketplace, and they know parents are very concerned in that way. And we think our GP channel will do it, too. So we will keep with our channel strategy and not go outside that from an OEM standpoint.

It is a premium product overall. When you look at it from a retainer standpoint, it won't hard to retain our business at all because it's just completely different functionality overall. It is very unique, as I mentioned. It's really the only truly 3D printed mouth guard that we know with this kind of unique resin, and we have a lot of, obviously, design flexibility in order to make it as comfortable and functional as we possibly can for athletes. And we like the idea that they can kind of design the mouth guard that they want, and we'll stay within those protective procedures for that particular sport. So I see this as just right in line with our channel strategy. It's right in line with our technical strategy with 3D printing. It's a big opportunity for us overall.

segments.speaker: Kevin Caliendo
paras: If I can ask a quick follow-up. I've got some soccer in hockey and football parents asking me to ask, is this something that you can strap on to a helmet because they always get lost and chewed upon?

segments.speaker: Joseph Hogan
paras: Kevin, I have 2 answers to that. One is we can 3D print that, we can make it any way you want to. So if you want to have a strap on it at [indiscernible], we could do that. But secondly, we plan to make these things so comfortable that kids aren't going to want to take them out of their mouth. A lot of time, what our research basically is they take it out because they can't speak. Oftenly, they can't swallow properly and they have to pull that out, they lose it on their helmet. So all right, that's again what we like this technology, we can design this in a different way because it is a higher-performance resin and a much more capable design criteria than what you could go with boil and bite and form and fill kind of mouth guards now.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: And we have reached the end of our question-and-answer session. I will now turn the call back over to Shirley Stacy for any closing remarks.

segments.speaker: Shirley Stacy
paras: Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We look forward to meeting and speaking with you at upcoming investor conferences and industry meetings. If you have any follow-up questions or need more information, please contact Align Investor Relations. Thanks, and have a great day.

segments.speaker: Operator
paras: Thank you. This concludes today's conference. And you may disconnect your lines at this time. Thank you for your participation.
